# error_path_targets.txt — the oracle-checked error-path call corpus for the
# `beam_engine` corpus error-path suite (`tests/exceptions_corpus.rs`,
# `corpus_error_paths_execute_and_agree_with_the_oracle`).
#
# Every non-comment line is
#
#     <module>:<function>/<arity>  <POISON>  =>  <EXPECTED>   # oracle: <erl command>
#
# `<expected>` is the exception the REAL system Erlang (OTP 29 / erts-17.1) raises for
# `Module:Function(<poison>)`; the trailing comment quotes the exact `erl -noshell -eval`
# invocation that reproduces it (copy-paste one line to re-verify).  No value here was
# guessed and none was derived from the Rust engine's own output: the whole file was
# derived by evaluating every expression in one real `erl` node under a spawn-with-watchdog
# harness (`apply(M,F,[Arg])`, 3 s per call, so a pathological input cannot stall it) and
# the per-line command below is the equivalent direct form.
#
# POISON   atom = the atom `genesis_poison` (matches no clause)   int = the small integer 7
#          nil  = []                                              tuple0 = {}
# EXPECTED function_clause  a BARE-atom reason (the failed-function-clause shape)
#          {tag}             a 2-tuple reason {tag, <poison>}; tag is `case_clause`,
#                            `badmatch` or `badrecord` (a failed case / match / record match)
#          unsupported       the engine must return a TYPED error instead — a documented gap
#                            (the call needs machinery the test host does not serve)
#
# Deterministic capping rule, so this file is reproducible from the sweep: for every corpus
# module the sweep reached, the file keeps the alphabetically-first `function_clause` target
# and the alphabetically-first tuple-reason target.  The complete un-capped sweep found 633
# `function_clause` + 99 tuple-reason calls that agree with the oracle, over these same 162
# modules.  Only the in-VM raise opcodes are used (`func_info` -> `function_clause`,
# `case_end`/`if_end`/`badmatch`/`badrecord`), i.e. mistakes the COMPILED CODE makes itself.

application:behaviour_info/1 atom => function_clause  # oracle: erl -noshell -eval 'try application:behaviour_info(genesis_poison) catch C:R -> io:format("~p:~p~n",[C,R]) end,halt().'
application_controller:is_running/1 int => function_clause  # oracle: erl -noshell -eval 'try application_controller:is_running(7) catch C:R -> io:format("~p:~p~n",[C,R]) end,halt().'
